evidence.snippet: if (!state || state.length < 16) { throw new Error('Invalid state parameter'); }
evidence.why: State is only checked for length, never compared against the value originally generated/stored for this auth attempt, so it is not actually validated against session (CSRF binding broken).

evidence.snippet: const codeChallenge = btoa(codeVerifier).substring(0, 43); // Simplified S256 challenge
evidence.why: Declares code_challenge_method S256 but sends base64 of the verifier instead of its SHA-256 hash, and the verifier itself is never persisted or sent during token exchange, so PKCE is not actually enforced end-to-end.

other_classes_observed: weak random state/verifier generation using Math.random (not cryptographically secure)
